Please pay attention and read carefully otherwise you could lose data! \n\nDon\'t worry, you can still change any of the options later in the Settings. To ensure the security of your accounts andOTP only stores them in encrypted data files. Here you can choose which method of encryption will be used. The KeyStore is a system component of Android for securely storing cryptographic keys. The advantage of this method is that the keys are stored separated from the data files and can be backed by hardware cryptography (if your device supports it). However, as the keys are not stored with the apps data, this method prevents external backup solutions (like Titanium) from working. If you choose this method you will have to rely on the internal backup functions provided by andOTP. \n\nWarning: The KeyStore is known to cause a lot of problems, please only use it if you absolutely have to. If you don\'t mind entering a password / PIN every time you start andOTP it is highly recommended to use the password-based encryption instead. This method will encrypt your data with a key generated from a password or PIN. The main advantage here is that this will work with external backup solutions (like Titanium) and is much less failure-prone than the KeyStore. However, you will have to enter your credentials every time you start andOTP. Here you can setup an authentication to lock andOTP. Since you have chosen Android KeyStore as encryption method this is optional. Here you can setup an authentication to lock andOTP. Since you have chosen Password / PIN as encryption method you need to set either a password or a PIN to proceed. Please set a password to continue! Please set a PIN to continue! Please confirm your password to continue! Please confirm your PIN to continue! Finished Your settings have been saved, you are all set to use andOTP now!

steps.message:
Build succeeds. Here's a summary of the fix:

## Diagnosis

Both reported problems live in `app/src/main/java/org/shadowice/flocke/andotp/Activities/IntroScreenActivity.java`:

**1. Slide 3 showed the wrong encryption method.**
`EncryptionFragment` defaults its spinner to `PASSWORD` and notifies the activity, which calls `AuthenticationFragment.updateEncryptionType()`. But that method only updated the description *if the view already existed*:

```java
if (desc != null) { ... }
```

During the initial `ViewPager` setup, the authentication slide's view doesn't exist yet, so the notification was silently dropped and the layout's hard-coded default text (`intro_slide3_desc_keystore`) stayed on screen — even though `PASSWORD` was selected. That's why only *changing* the spinner (KeyStore → Password) fixed the text. It also explains why the dropdown greying-out was correct: `isEnabled()` reads the field, which *was* updated.

**2. Red "Please set a password to continue" while KeyStore is selected.**
The authentication method was hard-coded to default to `PASSWORD` regardless of the encryption type, so picking "Android KeyStore" (where auth is optional) still landed on the mandatory-password auth method with an empty field.

## Changes

- Added a shared `DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION` constant so both fragments start from the same state (`AuthenticationFragment` previously initialized its field to `KEYSTORE` while the encryption spinner defaulted to `PASSWORD`).
- `AuthenticationFragment.onCreateView()` now applies the currently selected encryption type (`updateEncryptionType(encryptionType)`) once the views exist, so a change received before view creation is no longer lost.
- `updateEncryptionType()` returns early only for the "view not created" case, and for `KEYSTORE` it resets the auth method to `NONE` (matching "this is optional") — but only if no credentials were typed, so user input is never discarded. It also refreshes navigation to clear a stale red warning.
- `EncryptionFragment` now tracks the selected type in a field (used by `getEncryptionType()` and to restore the spinner), so the user's choice survives the view being destroyed/recreated by the `ViewPager`, and its description is set immediately instead of only via the asynchronous spinner callback.
- Updated the layouts' hard-coded placeholder texts to match the default (password-based) encryption, so nothing stale is shown before the code runs.
